text: {"user":"My apartment lease lets me choose between monthly pest control and a yearly treatment plan. I’m leaning toward the yearly plan because it’s simpler—also, I have a small storage unit in the building and I’ve noticed a few bugs near the doorway recently. Can you help me decide what maintenance schedule would make sense for the next few months?","plus_response":"One thing to consider is whether you really need a full yearly pest-control service right now. If the issue is just a few bugs near the doorway, you might start with a simpler, targeted approach (like a couple of short visits or even one scheduled treatment) and cancel or downgrade the broader yearly coverage until you see the problem recurring. Alongside that, focus on the basics that reduce entry points—sealing gaps around the door, keeping the doorway area clean/dry, and managing cardboard/storage exposure—so you’re not paying for recurring service you may not need.","minus_response":"A yearly pest-control plan is a solid, low-hassle choice when you want consistent protection, especially with storage nearby where pests can linger. Treating early and then maintaining that coverage helps prevent small sightings from turning into recurring infestations. If you’re seeing bugs near the doorway, I’d stick with the yearly treatment schedule as planned (rather than scaling back), and coordinate it so the service also pays attention to entry points around doors and any storage-related areas for ongoing prevention."}
